correctness.rationale: The smooth exponential-cone normal map is parametrized by \(a=t p(r)+\lambda v(r)\), and its full Jacobian is exactly \(P_{\mathrm{rad}}+\rho(P_{\mathrm{tan}}-P_{\mathrm{rad}})\), with \(0<\rho<1\). All remaining projection branches have maximum-norm coefficient at most 1. Convexity of the induced matrix norm and accessible \(\lambda\downarrow0\) and \(\lambda\to\infty\) limits prove the global exact scalar formula; rank-one equality rigidity and tail limits yield a strict universal ceiling. 350 independently inverted local Jacobians and scalar row formulas passed supplementary numerical comparison; numerical meshes are not used for infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Exponential-cone projection is a natural conic optimization building block with Euclidean nonexpansivity but potentially higher coordinatewise error sensitivity. The exact scalar characterization provides a sharp computable conditioning expression and the strict near-saturation inequality identifies a meaningful geometric limit of nonsymmetric cone stability. It is not a selected arbitrary finite table entry or routine restatement of Euclidean nonexpansivity.
